subject: Two or more sets of colour scales

messages.author: 59e24b23b6b00e9d
messages.subject: Two or more sets of colour scales
parts:
Hi,
I was wondering if there's a way to set two or more distinguished colour scales for one plot.
For instance, I'm trying to plot several time courses of different samples on one plot. I'd like the symbols of every time series to be in a smooth colour gradient but that each sample (each time series) to be distinguished from the others.
Ideally would be to be able to choose parts of one gradient but with breaks so that each sample gets a different part of the gradient.

Of course I'm aware of scale_colour_manual, but I'm trying to avoid that (too many samples and I wouldn't want to spend my time generating gradient, when others did a better job before me).

Suggestions are very appreciated
Roey

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Two or more sets of colour scales
parts: I believe it is still the case that two color scales in one plot is still not possible. If you have faceted plots you could make two separate plots and put them together with grid.arrange().

Something like this, probably:

scales::hue_pal(h = c(0, 360) + 15, c = 100, l = 65, h.start = 0,
direction = 1)

scales::seq_gradient_pal(low = "#132B43", high = "#56B1F7", space = "Lab")

RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set1")

HTH,

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Two or more sets of colour scales
parts:
You need to add the number of outputs to the scales:: helpers.

?hue_pal
scales::hue_pal(h = c(0, 360) + 15, c = 100, l = 65, h.start = 0,

direction = 1)(20)

?seq_gradient_pal
#and you have to supply a gradient to the gradient helper
x <- seq(0, 1, length = 25)
scales::seq_gradient_pal(low = "#132B43", high = "#56B1F7", space = "Lab")(x)

Very useful functions... thanks for pointing them out Baptiste.

Brandon
